root_cause.text: Integer overflow when computing `lba + range` in `sbc_execute_unmap()`, due to missing overflow check, allows the sum to wrap around on 64-bit addition and evade the device capacity bounds check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `lba + range < lba` guard before the existing bounds check; the CVE description explicitly states that the UNMAP bounds check lacks protection against wrapping on 64-bit overflow.

candidates.rationale: This goto statement is part of the error path that should be triggered when the bounds check fails. However, because the check on line 1190 can be bypassed by overflow, this statement may not be reached, making it indirectly related to the vulnerability.
Closing brace of the error-handling block. Not directly vulnerable, but part of the code structure that contains the vulnerable condition.

This is the directly vulnerable statement. The addition `lba + range` can overflow on 64-bit when both values are large, causing the sum to wrap around to a small number and bypass the capacity bounds check. Missing overflow check is the root cause.

This assignment sets the error return value when the bounds check fails. It is affected by the vulnerability because the check may not fail due to overflow, so this line may not execute, but it is not itself a cause.
Jump to the error label after setting the error code. Similar to the previous goto, it is part of the intended error path but may be skipped due to overflow bypass.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the condition that performs the integer addition lba + range. Without an overflow check, a large lba and range can cause the sum to wrap around, bypassing the capacity bounds check and allowing out-of-bounds access.
This assignment sets the error return when the bounds check fails. Due to the overflow bypass, this line may not execute, allowing the invalid UNMAP to proceed.
This goto statement jumps to the error path when the bounds check triggers. It is part of the intended fix but can be skipped if the check is bypassed by overflow.

This closing brace closes the if block for the bounds check. It is part of the control flow that should prevent out-of-bounds, but is only reached if the condition fails (which may not happen due to overflow).

This while loop iterates over UNMAP descriptors. The vulnerable addition occurs inside this loop, and without overflow protection, each descriptor's lba+range can be manipulated to exceed the device capacity.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `sbc_execute_unmap()` computes `lba + range` without any overflow check at line `if (lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)`. This allows integer overflow, where a large lba and range can wrap around, bypassing the bounds check and enabling out-of-bounds access. No mitigation such as checking if `range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) - lba` is present.
